mainTopic: Freeing a half-slave: the end of the משנה, and רבה and רב יוסף on whether a שטר or כסף can free half a slave
overview: This amud finishes the משנה about a person who is half slave and half free. בית שמאי show he cannot marry anyone, and staying single goes against פריה ורביה. So, for תיקון העולם, the master is forced to free him, and the slave writes a note for half his value. בית הלל accept this ruling. The גמרא then brings a ברייתא where רבי and חכמים argue whether a master can free only half his slave. רבה says they argue only about freeing with a שטר, and everyone agrees about כסף. רב יוסף says they argue only about כסף, and everyone agrees about a שטר. A ברייתא refutes רב יוסף on the שטר, but he can still hold that they argue about כסף too. The גמרא then tests both views against another ברייתא and against our משנה, and רבינא's answer for רב יוסף continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The half-slave cannot marry a free woman, and cannot stay single
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי continue their argument: the half-slave cannot marry a free woman, and he cannot stay unmarried, because the world was made for פריה ורביה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He can't marry a free woman, because half of him is still a slave. Should he just never marry? But the world was created only for having children, as the פסוק says: 'He did not create it to be empty; He formed it to be lived in.'
steps.whatsHappening: We are in the middle of בית שמאי's argument in the משנה. They show that the half-slave is stuck: there is nobody he is allowed to marry, and staying single is not an option.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just before this line, the משנה said he cannot marry a שפחה because half of him is free. Here it closes the other door: half of him is a slave, so a free woman is also forbidden. Staying single is rejected because פריה ורביה is the purpose of creation, so the current setup cannot be allowed to stand.

keyTerms.meaning: A free woman (not a slave)
Half of him is a slave
Should he stay idle (never marry)?
Having children, the מצוה to be fruitful and multiply

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the start of a new discussion. It continues בית שמאי's argument from the earlier part of the משנה, which already ruled out marrying a שפחה.

phrases.english: A free woman, it is impossible,
since half of him is still a slave.
Should he be idle?
phrases.notes: He means: should he just never marry at all?

phrases.english: But wasn't the world created
only for having children,
as it is said:
"He did not create it to be empty; He formed it to be lived in"!
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 45:18

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲלֹא לֹא נִבְרָא הָעוֹלָם אֶלָּא לִפְרִיָּה וּרְבִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues בית שמאי's argument from the earlier part of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A half-slave has no permitted marriage partner, and staying single goes against the purpose of creation.

steps.title: The solution: force the master to free him
steps.stepSummary: Because of תיקון העולם, the master is forced to free the half-slave, and the slave writes a note promising to pay half his value.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, for the betterment of the world, we force his master to make him a free man, and the slave writes a note owing the master half his value.
steps.whatsHappening: בית שמאי now give their practical ruling, which solves the problem they just raised.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The master is not simply robbed of his half. He gets a שטר חוב for the value of the half he still owned. This way the slave can marry and the master is paid back.

keyTerms.meaning: The betterment of the world, a reason the חכמים give for a ruling
We force
A free man
Half his value (his price)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the final הלכה of the משנה, since בית הלל end up agreeing to it.

phrases.english: Rather, for the betterment of the world
we force his master
and he makes him a free man,
and he writes a note for half his value.
phrases.notes: The slave writes this IOU to his master, to pay for the half the master still owned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the solution to the problem raised in step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The master is forced to free the half-slave, and the slave writes the master a note for half his value.

steps.title: בית הלל agree with בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל changed their ruling to follow בית שמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל went back to rule like בית שמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends by telling us that בית הלל gave up their earlier view and accepted בית שמאי's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, בית הלל said the half-slave should simply work one day for his master and one day for himself. After hearing בית שמאי's argument, they agreed that the master must free him.

keyTerms.meaning: And they went back on (changed) their view
To rule, to teach the הלכה

steps.whatToRemember: The final הלכה: a half-slave is not left half-and-half. His master is forced to free him, and he writes a note for half his value. This is one of the rare cases where בית הלל accept בית שמאי's view.

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel went back
to rule according to the words of Beit Shammai.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחָזְרוּ בֵּית הִלֵּל לְהוֹרוֹת כְּדִבְרֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the משנה by recording that בית הלל accepted the ruling in step 2
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows בית שמאי: the master is forced to free the half-slave.

steps.title: Can a master free only half his slave?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבי says freeing half a slave works, and חכמים say it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: If someone frees half of his slave, רבי says the slave has acquired his freedom for that half, and חכמים say he has not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by quoting a ברייתא that shows a מחלוקת about whether a master can free just half of his slave. This explains how the משנה's half-slave could come about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה assumed a slave can end up half free. Here we learn this is argued: according to רבי, freeing half works; according to חכמים, it has no effect.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
The Rabbis taught, the opening of a ברייתא
One who frees (a slave)
He acquired, meaning the freeing takes effect

phrases.english: Gemara
The Rabbis taught:
One who frees half of his slave,
Rabbi says: he has acquired,
phrases.notes: "Acquired" here means the slave really becomes free for that half.

phrases.english: and the Rabbis say: he has not acquired.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא with a ברייתא about how someone becomes half free
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי: freeing half a slave works. חכמים: it does not.

steps.title: רבה: the argument is only about freeing with a document
steps.stepSummary: רבה limits the מחלוקת to freeing with a שטר, and begins showing רבי's source from a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: The argument is only when the master frees the slave with a document. רבי's reason is the פסוק: 'And she has not been redeemed at all, nor was freedom given to her.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה explains exactly where רבי and חכמים argue. He then brings the פסוק that רבי relies on, which sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to free a slave: money (כסף) and a document (שטר). רבה says that with money, everyone agrees half can be freed. The only argument is about a שטר. The פסוק mentions both ways side by side: 'redeemed' is money, and 'freedom given' is a שטר.

keyTerms.meaning: A disagreement
A document, here a שטר שחרור (document of freedom)
She was redeemed (with money)
Freedom

steps.confusionAlert: רבה is not saying everyone agrees about a שטר. It is the reverse: with money, everyone agrees half works, and the argument is only about a שטר.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
The dispute is with a document,
for Rabbi holds:
"And she has not been redeemed at all,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:20. "Redeemed" means freed with money.

phrases.english: nor was freedom given to her"
phrases.notes: "Freedom given" means freed with a document.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the ברייתא's מחלוקת to freeing with a שטר and brings רבי's פסוק
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מחלוקת between רבי and חכמים is only about freeing with a שטר, not with money.

steps.title: The פסוק compares a document to money
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק puts שטר next to כסף. Just as money can free all or half of a slave, so can a document.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק compares a document to money. Just as money can free all of him or half of him, a document can also free all of him or half of him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה finishes explaining רבי's proof. Because the פסוק places the two ways of freeing together, they work the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a היקש: two things written together in a פסוק share the same rules. Everyone agrees a slave who pays half his value becomes half free. So according to רבי, a שטר can also free just half.

keyTerms.meaning: Compares (makes a היקש), learning one thing from another written next to it
Money
Whether all of him or half of him

steps.whyThisMatters: This היקש is the foundation of רבי's view. The גמרא next goes on to explain how חכמים see it.

phrases.english: It compares a document to money:
just as with money,
whether all of him or half of him,
so too with a document as well,
whether all of him or half of him;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק from step 5 proves רבי's view
steps.raayaObject: רבי's view that a שטר can free half a slave
steps.raayaSupportSource: A היקש from ויקרא 19:20, which places freeing with a שטר next to freeing with money

steps.title: The Rabbis learn from a woman's divorce that a document cannot free half a slave
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן use a גזירה שוה (the word 'לה' in both places) to compare freeing a slave to divorcing a woman. A גט cannot divorce half a woman, so a שטר cannot free half a slave. With כסף, everyone agrees half-freeing works.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן learn 'to her' and 'to her' from a woman: just as a woman cannot be half divorced, so too a slave cannot be half freed. But with money, everyone agrees it works: she is redeemed and not redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still inside רבה's explanation. Now it gives the source for the רבנן, who say a שטר cannot free half a slave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי compared שטר to כסף, because they sit next to each other in the פסוק. The רבנן instead link the slave's freedom to a woman's גט, because the same word 'לה' appears in both. Since you cannot give half a גט, you cannot give half a שטר of freedom. Freeing with כסף is not affected, so on כסף everyone agrees.

keyTerms.meaning: They learn (a law from a source)
'To her': the same word in both פסוקים, which makes the link
Half of him
Everyone agrees
Redeemed and not redeemed, meaning half-freed

steps.confusionAlert: In רבה's view, the argument is ONLY about a שטר. With כסף, even the רבנן agree you can free half a slave.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis learn 'to her' and 'to her' from a woman:
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:20 (about the slave) and דברים 24:1 (about the גט) both use the word 'לה'.

phrases.english: just as with a woman, half of her does not work,
so too with a slave, half of him does not work;
but with money, everyone agrees he acquires (half his freedom),
she is redeemed and not redeemed.
phrases.notes: This is how the פסוק's double wording 'והפדה לא נפדתה' gets read: half-redeemed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After giving רבי's source (step 6), רבה gives the רבנן's source.
steps.raayaObject: The רבנן's ruling that a שטר cannot free half a slave
steps.raayaSupportSource: A גזירה שוה from the word 'לה' in the פסוק about the slave and in the פסוק about the גט

steps.title: Is the argument about which kind of learning is stronger?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי and the רבנן disagree in general about whether a הקש or a גזירה שוה is the stronger tool.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say they argue about this: one holds a הקש is stronger, and the other holds a גזירה שוה is stronger?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a suggestion: maybe the real argument is about which kind of learning wins. It is setting up the next step, which will reject this idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי used a הקש (שטר placed next to כסף), and the רבנן used a גזירה שוה (the shared word 'לה'). So it looks like each side simply picks a different tool. If that were true, this would be a big, general argument that reaches far beyond slaves.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (a suggestion the גמרא may reject)
They disagree
A הקש: learning from two things placed next to each other in a פסוק
Learning from the same word used in two places
Is stronger / is preferred

phrases.english: Shall we say they argue about this:
that one master holds a הקש is stronger,
phrases.notes: This is רבי, who learned שטר from כסף.

phrases.english: and the other master holds a גזירה שוה is stronger?
phrases.notes: This is the רבנן, who learned from the word 'לה'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks at the two sources just given and asks whether the argument is really about which kind of learning is stronger.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the argument between רבי and the רבנן a general argument about הקש versus גזירה שוה?

steps.title: No: everyone prefers a גזירה שוה, but this one can be knocked down
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. Everyone agrees a גזירה שוה is stronger. רבי does not use it here only because a woman and a slave are different: a woman cannot leave her marriage with כסף, but a slave can go free with כסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone agrees a גזירה שוה is stronger. But here it is different, because the comparison can be knocked down: a woman cannot go out with money, so how can you compare her to a slave, who can go out with money?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the idea from the last step. The argument is not about which tool is stronger in general.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי agrees that a גזירה שוה usually wins. But a comparison only works if the two cases are alike. A woman is never freed by כסף and a slave is, so the link between them is weak. That is why רבי falls back on the הקש.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
Here it is different
To knock down (to point out a difference that breaks a comparison)
What about X, which has this special feature? (a way of breaking a comparison)

steps.whyThisMatters: It keeps the argument narrow. רבי does not reject the general rule that a גזירה שוה is stronger; he only says this particular one breaks down.

phrases.aramaic: לָא; דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה עֲדִיפָא,
phrases.english: No; everyone agrees a גזירה שוה is stronger,
but here it is different, because the comparison can be knocked down:

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְאִשָּׁה שֶׁכֵּן אֵינָהּ יוֹצְאָה בְּכֶסֶף,
phrases.english: what about a woman? She cannot go out (of a marriage) with money,
so can you say the same about a slave, who does go out with money?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא; דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה עֲדִיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the argument is a general one about הקש versus גזירה שוה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The גזירה שוה here is weak, because a woman cannot leave her marriage with כסף while a slave can go free with כסף

steps.title: רב יוסף: the argument is about money, and with a document no one can free half
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף disagrees with רבה. He says רבי and the רבנן argue about freeing with כסף. רבי learns half-redemption from the double wording 'והפדה לא נפדתה', while the רבנן say the Torah speaks like people talk. With a שטר, everyone agrees half-freeing does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: The argument is about money. רבי holds that 'והפדה לא נפדתה' means redeemed and not redeemed. The רבנן hold that the תורה speaks in the way people speak. But with a document, everyone agrees it does not work.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a different explanation from רבה about where the argument between רבי and the רבנן lies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה said the argument was about a שטר and everyone agreed about כסף; רב יוסף says the exact opposite. For רבי, the doubled verb 'והפדה... נפדתה' teaches half-redemption with כסף. The רבנן say a doubled verb is just normal speech and teaches nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument / disagreement
'And she was not fully redeemed' (ויקרא 19:20), with the verb doubled
The Torah speaks in the way people normally speak, so a doubled word is not a hint
A written document (here, a document of freedom)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two views. רבה: they argue about a שטר, and everyone agrees about כסף. רב יוסף: they argue about כסף, and everyone agrees about a שטר.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to explain the argument between רבי and the רבנן. רבה puts it in שטר; רב יוסף puts it in כסף. In each view, the other method has full agreement. Steps 11-12 show that רב יוסף's claim about a שטר is refuted.

phrases.english: And Rav Yosef said: The argument is about money,
for Rabbi holds: 'And she was not redeemed at all'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:20. The Hebrew says the word 'redeem' twice.

phrases.english: means redeemed and not redeemed;

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבָּנַן סָבְרִי: דִּבְּרָה תּוֹרָה כִּלְשׁוֹן בְּנֵי אָדָם;
phrases.english: and the Rabbis hold: The Torah spoke in the language of people;
phrases.notes: So the doubled word is just normal speech, not a hint for a new law.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בִּשְׁטָר – דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל לֹא קָנָה.
phrases.english: but with a document, everyone agrees he does not acquire (half his freedom).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second explanation of the ברייתא in step 4 that disagrees with רבה (steps 5-9).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument between רבי and the רבנן is about freeing with כסף. With a שטר, everyone agrees half-freeing does not work.

steps.title: A ברייתא contradicts רב יוסף
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says רבי and the חכמים argue about freeing half a slave with a שטר. That contradicts רב יוסף, who said everyone agrees a שטר cannot free half a slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him from a ברייתא: someone frees half his slave with a document. רבי says the slave goes free, and the חכמים say he does not. This is a refutation of רב יוסף!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יוסף with a ברייתא that shows a real argument about half-freeing a slave with a שטר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף said the argument is only about כסף, and that with a שטר everyone agrees half-freeing does not work. But this ברייתא clearly has רבי saying a שטר does work for half a slave. That fits רבה's view, not רב יוסף's.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (usually from a ברייתא)
One who frees (a slave)
Acquired, meaning here that the slave gained his freedom

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
One who frees half of his slave with a document,
Rabbi says: he has acquired [his freedom],
phrases.notes: He means the slave is now half free.

phrases.english: and the Sages say: he has not acquired [it].
This is a refutation of Rav Yosef!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב יוסף's view from step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that everyone agrees half-freeing with a שטר does not work
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא shows רבי holding that a שטר does free half a slave, so the two sides really do argue about a שטר.

steps.title: רב יוסף is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that רב יוסף is refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is indeed a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits that the challenge stands and רב יוסף's view is rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no answer for רב יוסף, so his claim that everyone agrees about a שטר falls: רבי and the חכמים really do argue about a שטר. This does not prove רבה's claim about כסף. Steps 13-14 show רב יוסף can still hold that they argue about כסף too.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation. Said a second time, it means the refutation is final.

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא proves that רבי and the חכמים argue about freeing half a slave with a שטר. רב יוסף's claim that everyone agrees about a שטר is rejected.

phrases.english: It is indeed a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of step 11
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב יוסף is refuted. The dispute is about half-freeing with a שטר.

steps.title: Is רב יוסף refuted twice?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists the argument only for a שטר. That seems to mean everyone agrees about כסף, which would refute רב יוסף on a second point too.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is with a document that they argue, but with money they do not argue. Shall we say this is a refutation of רב יוסף on two points?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the ברייתא also implies that there is no argument about כסף, which would be a second strike against רב יוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף said the חכמים hold that half-freeing with כסף does not work. If the ברייתא means that with כסף 'they do not argue', then the חכמים agree it works. That would make רב יוסף wrong about כסף as well.

keyTerms.meaning: That they argue
Shall we say
On two points

phrases.english: (Let us say) it is with a document that they argue,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some leave it out.

phrases.english: but with money they do not argue;
shall we say it should be a refutation
of Rav Yosef on two points!
phrases.notes: Point one is about the document. Point two is that רב יוסף said the חכמים argue about money too.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא תֶּיהְוֵי תְּיוּבְתָּא דְּרַב יוֹסֵף בְּתַרְתֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a further inference from the same ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that the חכמים reject half-freeing with כסף
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Because the ברייתא names only a שטר, it seems everyone agrees that כסף does work for half a slave.

steps.title: The argument covers money too
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף could answer that the argument applies to כסף too. It is taught about a שטר only to show how far רבי's view goes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף could tell you: they argue about a document, and the same is true about money. They are shown arguing about a document to teach you how far רבי's view goes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב יוסף on the second point. Not mentioning כסף does not mean everyone agrees about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים say no to half-freeing even with כסף. The ברייתא picked the שטר case because that is where רבי's lenient view is most surprising. רבי allows half-freeing even with a שטר, and all the more so with כסף.

keyTerms.meaning: And the same is true
To show you his strength, meaning how far his view goes

steps.confusionAlert: This defends רב יוסף only against the second point. He is still refuted on the first point, from step 12.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef could say to you:
They argue about a document, and the same is true about money.
And the reason they are shown arguing about a document
is to show you how far Rabbi's view goes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'double refutation' of step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why the ברייתא chose this case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Mentioning only a שטר means there is no argument about כסף.
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument covers כסף too. The שטר case was chosen to show how far רבי's lenient view goes.

steps.title: Why not show the חכמים' strength instead?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא did not teach the argument about כסף, which would show how far the חכמים' strict view goes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let them argue about money instead, and show you how far the חכמים' view goes!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer just given. Either case could highlight one side, so why highlight רבי?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the argument were taught about כסף, it would show that the חכמים forbid half-freeing even with כסף, which is the stronger method. That would show how far the strict view goes, just as the שטר case shows how far the lenient view goes.

keyTerms.meaning: Let them argue
The strength of the רבנן's view

phrases.english: Let them argue about money,
and show you how far the Rabbis' view goes!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא chose the שטר case to show רבי's strength
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא could just as well have chosen the כסף case to show the חכמים' strength.

steps.title: Showing a lenient view is preferred
steps.stepSummary: A תנא prefers to show how far a lenient view goes, so the ברייתא taught the שטר case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Showing the strength of a lenient view is preferable to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the תנא prefers to highlight the lenient opinion, which here is רבי's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'no' needs no special basis. A lenient ruling is a bold claim, though, so showing how far it reaches teaches more. That is why the ברייתא chose the case that shows רבי's leniency.

keyTerms.meaning: The strength of a lenient view
Is preferable

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא refutes רב יוסף about the שטר. But he can still hold that the argument covers כסף too, because the ברייתא chose the שטר case to show the strength of רבי's lenient view.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a common rule across ש״ס: when a תנא chooses which case to teach, he prefers the one that shows how far a lenient view goes.

phrases.english: Showing the strength of a lenient view is preferable to him.
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the תנא who taught the ברייתא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: A general rule about how a תנא chooses which case to teach
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Either case would be an equally good choice.
steps.terutzMaskana: A lenient view is better to highlight, so the שטר case was chosen.

steps.title: A ברייתא: half-redemption with money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that reads the double phrase "והפדה לא נפדתה" as describing a maidservant who is half redeemed, through כסף or שוה כסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: "And redeemed." Could it mean fully redeemed? The פסוק says "not redeemed." If "not redeemed," could it mean not redeemed at all? The פסוק says "and redeemed." So how does it work? She is redeemed and not redeemed, meaning half redeemed, through money or something worth money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new source, a ברייתא, to help decide the argument between רבה and רב יוסף. This first part sets up the basic idea that a maidservant can be half redeemed with money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses two opposite words, "redeemed" and "not redeemed." Neither word alone can be the full picture, so the ברייתא says she must be partly redeemed. It then states that this happens through כסף or שוה כסף.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear. It introduces a source brought as a proof.
"And redeemed, not redeemed." This is the double phrase from the פסוק.
The פסוק teaches us
Redeemed and not redeemed, meaning half redeemed
Something worth money

phrases.english: Come and hear: "And redeemed";
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:20

phrases.english: might it mean fully redeemed?
The verse says: "not redeemed."
If "not redeemed," might it mean not redeemed at all?
The verse says: "and redeemed."
So how does it work? Redeemed and not redeemed;
through money or something worth money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new proof source about the רבה and רב יוסף argument, now that the discussion of the earlier ברייתא is finished.
steps.raayaObject: Which view of the argument between רבי and the חכמים is correct, רבה's or רב יוסף's

steps.title: The ברייתא adds freeing with a document
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from the גט of divorce that a maidservant can also be freed with a שטר, not only with money.
steps.simpleTranslation: I only know about money. How do I know about a document? The פסוק says "and not redeemed, or freedom was not given to her." Later it says "and he writes her a scroll of severance." Just as there it is done with a document, here too it can be done with a document.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and adds a second way to free her: a שטר, a written document of freedom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Money was already taught. Now the ברייתא compares the freedom in our פסוק to a גט, which is a written document. So a document can also give freedom.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know?
Freedom
A scroll of severance, meaning a גט
Just as there, so too here. This is how a comparison is drawn.

phrases.english: And I only know about money;
how do I know about a document?
The verse says: "And not redeemed,
or freedom was not given to her,"
and later on it says:
"And he writes her a scroll of severance" –
phrases.notes: דברים 24:1

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְהַלָּן בִּשְׁטָר, אַף כָּאן בִּשְׁטָר.
phrases.english: just as there it is with a document, so too here it is with a document.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין לִי אֶלָּא בְּכֶסֶף, בִּשְׁטָר מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא and adds שטר alongside כסף.
steps.raayaObject: Which view of the argument between רבי and the חכמים is correct
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא, comparing ויקרא 19:20 to דברים 24:1

steps.title: The ברייתא adds half-freeing with a document
steps.stepSummary: By placing שטר next to כסף in the same פסוק, the ברייתא teaches that a document can free half a slave, just as money can.
steps.simpleTranslation: I only know that half can be freed with money, or all with a document. How do I know that half can be freed with a document? The פסוק says "and not redeemed, or freedom was not given to her." It compares a document to money. Just as money works for all or for half, a document also works for all or for half.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by teaching that even a שטר can free half of a slave. This is the key line for the debate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק mentions redemption (money) and freedom (document) together. That puts them side by side, so the rules of money carry over to a document. Money can free half, so a document can free half too.

keyTerms.meaning: Half of him
All of him
He compares. Two things placed together in one פסוק share the same rules.

steps.whatToRemember: The last line of the ברייתא says that half of a slave can be freed even with a שטר. That is רבי's view.

phrases.english: I only know about half of him with money,
or all of him with a document;
how do I know about half of him with a document?

phrases.aramaic: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וְהׇפְדֵּה לֹא נִפְדָּתָה אוֹ חוּפְשָׁה לֹא נִתַּן לָהּ״ –
phrases.english: The verse says: "And not redeemed, or freedom was not given to her" –
it compares a document to money:

phrases.aramaic: מָה כֶּסֶף בֵּין כּוּלּוֹ בֵּין חֶצְיוֹ,
phrases.english: just as money works for all of him or half of him,

phrases.aramaic: אַף שְׁטָר נָמֵי בֵּין כּוּלּוֹ בֵּין חֶצְיוֹ.
phrases.english: so too a document works for all of him or half of him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא חֶצְיוֹ בְּכֶסֶף, אוֹ כּוּלּוֹ בִּשְׁטָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the ברייתא by extending half-freeing from כסף to שטר.
steps.raayaObject: Which view of the argument between רבי and the חכמים is correct
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's comparison of שטר to כסף in ויקרא 19:20

steps.title: The ברייתא fits רב יוסף but is awkward for רבה
steps.stepSummary: After his refutation, רב יוסף holds that they argue about both money and documents, so the whole ברייתא is רבי. For רבה, the first part would be everyone's view and the last part only רבי's, which is awkward.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for רב יוסף after he was refuted: whose view is this? It is רבי. But for רבה, is the first part everyone's view and the last part רבי's?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the ברייתא to challenge רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After his refutation, רב יוסף holds that רבי and the חכמים argue about both כסף and שטר. So the whole ברייתא is simply רבי's view. רבה holds that everyone agrees half can be freed with כסף. That makes the money part everyone's view and the document part only רבי's, splitting one ברייתא between two views.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well for...
After he was refuted
Whose view is this?
The first part and the last part of a source
Everyone's view

steps.confusionAlert: Here רב יוסף means his updated view after the refutation (they argue about both). It is not his original position.

phrases.english: It works well for רב יוסף after he was refuted:
phrases.notes: After being refuted, he holds they argue about money and documents alike.

phrases.english: whose view is this? It is רבי.
But for רבה –
is the first part everyone's view, and the last part רבי?!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַב יוֹסֵף בָּתַר דְּאִיתּוֹתַב, הָא מַנִּי – רַבִּי הִיא. אֶלָּא לְרַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ברייתא from steps 17-19 to the two views and challenges רבה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's view that everyone agrees half can be freed with כסף
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A single ברייתא should follow one view. Under רבה it would have to be split, with its first part as everyone's view and its last part as רבי's alone.

steps.title: רבה accepts that the ברייתא is split between two views
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that the first part of the ברייתא (money) is everyone's view, and the last part (a document) is only רבי's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה could say to you: Yes, the first part is everyone's view, and the last part is רבי's view.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the קשיא from step 20 by accepting the split: he says a ברייתא can begin with something everyone agrees on and end with a view that only רבי holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge was that splitting one ברייתא between two views is awkward. רבה simply says 'yes,' and the split is fine. Freeing half a slave with money is accepted by all, and freeing half with a שטר is only רבי's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
The first part (of a ברייתא or משנה)
The last part (of a ברייתא or משנה)
Everyone's view, accepted by all

phrases.english: Rabba could say to you:
Yes, the first part is everyone's view,
phrases.notes: The first part is freeing half a slave with money.

phrases.english: and the last part is Rabbi's view.
phrases.notes: The last part is freeing half a slave with a document, a שטר.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר לך רבה: אין, רישא דברי הכל, וסיפא רבי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא in step 20 by accepting the split between the first part and the last part.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the split: a ברייתא may combine a view everyone holds with a view only one תנא holds.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought one ברייתא could not reasonably be split between everyone's view and רבי's view.
steps.terutzMaskana: The split is acceptable. Money is everyone's view, and a שטר is only רבי's view.

steps.title: רב אשי says the whole ברייתא follows רבי
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a different answer: the entire ברייתא is רבי's teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: It is רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the same קשיא in another way. He says the whole ברייתא is רבי's teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה split the ברייתא into two parts. רב אשי avoids the split and says the whole ברייתא comes from רבי. The awkwardness of mixing two views in one ברייתא then disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who offers a different answer here
It follows רבי (רבי יהודה הנשיא)

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
It is Rabbi's view.
phrases.notes: He means the whole ברייתא, both parts, is רבי's teaching.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another answer to the קשיא of step 20, different from רבה's answer in step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the whole source to one תנא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the ברייתא had to be split between everyone's view and רבי's view.
steps.terutzMaskana: The entire ברייתא is רבי's teaching, so it is not split.

steps.title: The משנה about a half-free slave challenges רב יוסף
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה speaks about a slave who is half free. רבה can say this happened through money, which everyone accepts. But for רב יוסף, should we say the משנה follows only רבי and not the רבנן?
steps.simpleTranslation: But our משנה teaches: 'One who is half slave and half free.' This works well for רבה, because he explains it as a case of money, and that is everyone's view. But for רב יוסף, should we say the משנה is only רבי's view and not the רבנן's?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now challenges רב יוסף. It points out that our משנה takes half freedom for granted. According to רב יוסף, only רבי allows that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה holds that everyone agrees money can free half a slave, so he can read the משנה as a money case that all accept. רב יוסף holds that the רבנן reject half freedom completely, whether by money or by a שטר. For him, the משנה would follow only רבי, and the גמרא does not want a plain משנה to go against the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Half slave and half free
It works well for (introduces the side that has no problem)
He explains it as speaking about a specific case
Shall we say? (raises an unwanted conclusion)

steps.confusionAlert: This challenge goes against רב יוסף, not רבה. In the previous steps רבה was the one under pressure. Now the משנה works easily for רבה and is hard for רב יוסף.
steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא prefers to explain a משנה so that it fits the רבנן as well, not just one תנא. A reading that makes the משנה follow only רבי is a real weakness.

phrases.english: But the Mishnah that teaches:

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁחֶצְיוֹ עֶבֶד וְחֶצְיוֹ בֶּן חוֹרִין;
phrases.english: One who is half slave and half free;
It works well according to Rabba:
he explains it as a case of money, and that is everyone's view;
phrases.notes: The slave was half redeemed with money, which רבה says everyone accepts.

phrases.english: But according to Rav Yosef:
shall we say it is Rabbi's view and not the Rabbis'?!
phrases.notes: For רב יוסף, the רבנן never allow half freedom, not with money and not with a שטר.

steps.triggerLanguage: אלא מתניתין דקתני: מי שחציו עבד וחציו בן חורין; בשלמא לרבה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רבה, the גמרא turns to a challenge against רב יוסף, using our משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's view that the רבנן reject half freedom even with money.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Our משנה assumes a slave can be half free. According to רב יוסף, only רבי holds this. So the plain משנה would go against the רבנן, which is unlikely. רבה avoids this by reading the משנה as a money case.

steps.title: רבינא begins his answer for רב יוסף
steps.stepSummary: רבינא begins to answer the challenge against רב יוסף. His words continue on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא introduces רבינא, who will answer the challenge against רב יוסף, and his actual answer comes right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far only the name of the speaker appears. The content of רבינא's answer, which explains how the משנה can fit רב יוסף's view, comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who answers the challenge against רב יוסף

phrases.english: Ravina said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces the answer to the קשיא of step 23 against רב יוסף.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Not yet stated. The answer continues in the next section.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the משנה must follow only רבי according to רב יוסף.
steps.terutzMaskana: Pending. רבינא's explanation comes in the continuation.
